note: Page Specific Class adds CSS classes to the <body> tag per page via a single hook_preprocess_html(). Its entire state is one config value: page_specific_class.settings.url_with_class, a multi-line string of '/<path>|<class(es)>' rules (supports /<front>, /*, and '/prefix*' wildcards). Config UI at route page_specific_class.settings (/admin/config/page-class/settings, permission 'administer site configuration'). No plugins/permissions-of-its-own/Drush. All medium/hard cases are grounded in that real config value: introspection reads a known url_with_class mapping; execution writes a mapping and a verify parses url_with_class from live config. Baseline: url_with_class empty.

evals.prompt: Using the Drupal page_specific_class module, how do I add the CSS class 'special' to the body tag on the page /node/1? What config value and format does it use?
evals.expected_output: Add a line '/node/1|special' to page_specific_class.settings.url_with_class (via the settings form at /admin/config/page-class/settings, or drush cset). Each line is '/<path>|<class(es)>'; the path must start with '/' and path/class are separated by '|'.

evals.prompt: In page_specific_class, how do I add a body class to the front page only, to every page, and to all pages under a path prefix like /products?
evals.expected_output: Front page: '/<front>|home-class'. Every page: '/*|all-class'. Wildcard prefix: '/products*|products-class' (matches any path starting with /products). One rule per line.

evals.prompt: Which config object and key does page_specific_class store its path-to-class mappings in, and by what mechanism does it actually add the class to the page?
evals.expected_output: It stores mappings in page_specific_class.settings under the key url_with_class (a multi-line string). hook_preprocess_html() reads it and appends matching class(es) to the body via $variables['attributes']['class'].

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, page_specific_class is configured so that a particular page gets a body class. Inspect the live configuration and report which CSS class is added to the body on the page /node/1.
evals.expected_output: page_specific_class.settings.url_with_class contains the line '/node/1|psc-known-class', so the body class added on /node/1 is psc-known-class.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, page_specific_class has a wildcard rule configured. Inspect the live configuration and report which body class is applied to pages under /pscarticles.
evals.expected_output: page_specific_class.settings.url_with_class contains '/pscarticles*|psc-wild', so any path starting with /pscarticles gets the body class psc-wild.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, use the page_specific_class module to add the CSS class 'psc-eval-class' to the body tag on the page at path /psc-eval-page. Apply the change to the live site configuration.
evals.expected_output: page_specific_class.settings.url_with_class contains a line '/psc-eval-page|psc-eval-class' (added via the settings form or drush cset).

evals.prompt: On my Drupal site I want the home page's <body> tag to have the class 'psc-home' so I can style the front page differently. Set this up on the live site using the page classes tool.
evals.expected_output: page_specific_class.settings.url_with_class contains a line '/<front>|psc-home' (the /<front> token targets the front page).
